newsitem.title: CANADA: ATHLETICS-BAILEY SHOWS TOP FORM AT HARRY JEROME CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAILEY SHOWS TOP FORM AT HARRY JEROME CLASSIC.

text.p: Olympic champion Donovan Bailey served notice that he is primed for his June 1 sprint showdown against Michael Johnson by posting the second-fastest 100 meters in the world this year on Sunday.

Bailey, who holds the world record at 9.84 seconds, eased to victory at the Harry Jerome Track Classic at Swangard Stadium in a time of 9.99 seconds, then anchored the Canadian relay team in a relaxed victory.
The Canadian later pronounced himself pleased but not entirely satisfied with his form going into his 150-meter match race with double-Olympic champion Johnson of the United States at the SkyDome.

"My transition wasn't as smooth as I wanted and the only way you can detect that is to run in a race," Bailey told the Canadian Press news agency after beating American Leroy Burrell. Burrell, whose world record Bailey took at the Altanta Games, was second in 10.18.

"My speed is still there but the transition and relaxation aren't but it's just my second race of the year," Bailey added. "My finish in Brazil (two weeks ago, when he ran 10.13) was good and the first part of the race wasn't.
"I'll put it all together one of these days."
Only Ato Boldon of Trinidad, who ran 9.89 in Japan last week, has been faster this season.
"Any time you go under 10 seconds at any time in a season, you feel good," Bailey said.

The relay team, which consisted of Bailey, Glenroy Gilbert, Bruny Surin and Robert Esmie, won with a time of 38.97 seconds. The Olympic gold medalists were running for the first time since Atlanta and have their sights set on the world record of 37.40.
